Scenic Highway
Has Waited.

One empty lot. A city deciding what comes next.

Chapter One  ·  Why Scotlandville Matters

This Is Not Empty Ground.

Southern University has anchored this ground for more than a century. Ethel's Snack Shack fed it. Harding Boulevard housed its businesses. Families raised children two and three generations deep on these blocks.

Then investment moved elsewhere, and never fully came back.

Southern University Commencement  ·  June 1952

Southern Built Scotlandville First.

Generation after generation gathered on this ground to send its best into a world that had not yet decided to receive them. They went anyway.

A university doesn't just educate a place. It commits to it.

Ethel's Snack Shack  ·  Scotlandville

Every Block Had a Name.

Red beans and rice, the original recipe, the same phone number for decades. A neighborhood institution — the kind that doesn't make history books, and doesn't need to.

Scotlandville was never anonymous. It just stopped being invested in.

Southern University  ·  Scotlandville, Louisiana  ·  Est. 1880

The University Stayed.

One institution kept its promise to this ground. The neighborhood around it is still waiting on everyone else.

Chapter Two  ·  The Opportunity

$22 Million. One Corner.

Build Baton Rouge has proposed a $22 million mixed-use development on Scenic Highway, beside the Cadence Apartments and Southern University.

Deidre Deculus Robert, President and CEO, is leading the effort. Jay Gaudet is driving the vision on the ground. Completion is targeted for summer 2028.

Nothing is built yet. That's what this book is for.

Conceptual Visualization

Here's What Could Stand Here.

Not a rendering of a specific building — an honest picture of what's possible when a corridor gets reinvested in, block by block.

The future rarely arrives. It reveals itself.

Chapter Three  ·  A Day in Scotlandville, 2030

Picture Tuesday.

Not a groundbreaking. Not a ribbon-cutting.

An ordinary evening, five years from now.

Conceptual Visualization

Porch Lights On.

Bikes on the sidewalk. Dinner outside because the evening's too good to eat indoors. Neighbors who've known each other three years, not thirty — and it already feels like it doesn't matter.

Extraordinary places succeed when they become ordinary parts of people's lives.

Chapter Four  ·  Visual Chapters

What Comes Back.

Streets people walk. Storefronts people run. Parks people take their kids to.

Not amenities — a neighborhood.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Housing

Room for Everyone.

A starter cottage and a family home, on the same block. Single-family and small multifamily, built to the same standard.

A starter home and a family home on the same block is not a compromise. It's a neighborhood.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Retail

A Storefront, Not a Suite.

Glass that faces the sidewalk. Light that spills out after dark. Retail built for a neighborhood, not a highway exit.

Retail that faces the sidewalk invites the sidewalk in.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Green Space

Shade That Waits for Them.

The oaks are already here. A neighborhood park doesn't need to be invented — it needs to be given somewhere to stand.

The oaks were already here. Everything else just has to catch up.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Local Business

Somebody's Name Is on the Door.

An entrepreneur doesn't need permission to believe in a block. They need a block worth believing in — and a storefront they can afford to open.

A market only becomes real once someone's willing to bet their name on it.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Evening

The Street Stays Lit.

String lights over a porch. Neighbors still outside after dinner. A block that doesn't empty out the second the sun goes down.

A neighborhood that's alive at 8pm is a neighborhood people choose.

Conceptual Visualization  ·  Public Art

The Culture Was Never Missing.

Scotlandville's history and Southern's legacy, painted where people actually walk — not filed away in an archive.

You don't install culture. You give it a wall.

Chapter Five  ·  Economic Impact

Ownership, Not Just Occupancy.

The plan includes lower-interest home loans and down payment assistance for buyers who commit to Scotlandville.

It includes student loan forgiveness for Southern graduates who stay and build their lives here — turning the university's biggest export back into the neighborhood's biggest asset.

Conceptual Visualization

Every New Resident Is a Vote of Confidence.

A market only becomes real once someone's willing to bet their mortgage on it. Ownership is the strongest form of belief a neighborhood can attract.

A market only becomes real once someone's willing to bet their mortgage on it.

Chapter Six  ·  Why It Works

Confidence Is Contagious.

Residents need to believe it's safe to stay. Developers need to believe the market is real. Lenders need to believe the collateral holds. Officials need to believe the votes are there.

One project, done right, can move all four at once.
